answer: To keep a jade market from becoming a haven for fake borrowers, its settlement bridge locks coins equal to each invoice before releasing goods. Validators bind each pledge to one invoice and reject coins already pledged. A hundred aliases with 100 coins can incur at most 100 coins of debt. On default, verified delivery lets the seller claim that invoice's escrow once. Honest buyers also tie up capital. Safety depends on valid delivery proofs and escrow that pays in the debt currency.
